links.outcome: Fairness metrics and discriminatory performance of FAIM versus common bias mitigation methods for hospital admission prediction
links.effect: FAIM models showed satisfactory discriminatory performance and significantly mitigated bias on fairness metrics, outperforming commonly used bias mitigation methods in both datasets. No numeric values in the abstract.
links.quote: For both datasets, FAIM models not only exhibit satisfactory discriminatory performance but also significantly mitigate biases as measured by well-established fairness metrics, outperforming commonly used bias mitigation methods.

unlisted_practices: Interactive interface for selecting a fairer model from a set of similarly high-performing models, with domain expert input

screen.reason: Empirical study evaluating FAIM, a fairness-aware interpretable modeling interface that allows domain experts to select fairer models and mitigate algorithmic bias in clinical risk prediction using retrospective ED databases.
